primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome (including severe dyslipidaemia, prediabetes, hypertension)
nice_guideline_used: CG181/PH46/NG28 (dyslipidaemia & prediabetes), NG136 (hypertension), NG28 (metformin), NG107/NG203 (anaemia/CKD considerations)

medications.purpose: Essential hypertension; renoprotective if CKD present
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive

medications.purpose: Essential hypertension; part of first‑line ACE‑I + thiazide regimen
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends low‑dose thiazide with ACE‑I

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3‑6 months then annually
medications.purpose: Severe dyslipidaemia (LDL‑C 193 mg/dL) to achieve ≥40% LDL‑C reduction and target <1.8 mmol/L
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46/NG28: high‑intensity statin for LDL‑C >190 mg/dL

medications.dose: 500 mg oral tablet once daily with evening meal, titrate to 500 mg twice daily after 2 weeks, then up to 1 g twice daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review HbA1c and renal function annually
medications.purpose: Prediabetes/high cardiovascular risk to prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (BMI ≥35 kg/m² or other risk factors)

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazides can modestly increase statin plasma concentrations, raising risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Counsel patient to report muscle pain; check CK if symptomatic; consider CK monitoring at 3 months

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant interaction; thiazide may slightly raise glucose but metformin counteracts

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² (risk of lactic acidosis)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR 30‑45, start at 500 mg once daily and monitor renal function; hold if eGFR <30

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in active liver disease or ALT >3× ULN
contraindications.alternative: Obtain baseline LFTs; if abnormal, consider lower‑intensity statin (e.g., rosuvastatin 20 mg) after review

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73m² for initial metformin prescribing; renal function must be measured before start and annually thereafter.
Liver function tests not provided – required before initiating high‑intensity statin.
BMI, waist circumference, smoking status, alcohol intake, and family history not documented – needed for full metabolic‑syndrome risk stratification.
Allergy status unknown – verify no hypersensitivity to statins or metformin.
No current CK or muscle symptom data – baseline CK advisable given high‑intensity statin.
treatment_summary: Start high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg daily and metformin MR 500 mg daily (titrating to target dose) to address severe dyslipidaemia and high‑risk prediabetes, while continuing the existing ACE‑I and low‑dose thiazide regimen for hypertension. Monitor renal function, liver enzymes, and CK levels; review blood pressure, lipids, and HbA1c at 3‑6 months and then annually. Provide lifestyle advice (weight loss, diet, exercise, smoking cessation) per NICE CG181/PH46 recommendations.
